decision.location: Abstract, lines 26-31; see also Introduction and Materials and methods, lines 79-98, and References 17-19, lines 270-279
decision.quote:
Recently, significant linkage has been
reported to a 39.5 cM region on the long arm of chromosome 2 (2q36-37; PARK11) in North American
Parkinson families under an autosomal dominant model of inheritance. We have performed a replication
study to confirm linkage to this region in a European population. Linkage analysis in 153 individuals from
45 European families with a strong family history of PD did not show any significant LOD score in this
region. Therefore, PARK11 does not seem to play a major role for familial PD in the European population.
decision.reason: Prestel et al. (2005, 10.1038/sj.ejhg.5201317) perform a replication of the North American PARK11 (chromosome 2q36-37) autosomal dominant linkage finding reported by Pankratz et al. Across References 17 (Pankratz et al. 2002, initial genome screen in 160 multiplex families), 18 (Pankratz et al. 2003b, Am J Hum Genet 72:1053-1057, 10.1086/374383, subset of 65 pedigrees with a strong family history of PD from the expanded cohort showing maximum LOD 5.1 at D2S206 across the 39.5 cM D2S126-D2S125 region under an autosomal dominant model), and 19 (Pankratz et al. 2003a, Hum Mol Genet 12:2599-2608, candidate target_index 1, confirming the same 2q36-37 linkage with LOD 4.9 in a further enlarged sample of 85 families / 113 sibling pairs with a strong family history of PD within 362 multiplex families), the same author group reported successive sample-expansion waves of the same North American multiplex PD family cohort and PARK11 linkage finding. As confirmed in the existing prior adjudication file (7856b4943e3474405c39939704c1a1e14ac0756d564e9f17e5197e5591d5e0b0.json; prior state file e8d9d11abbb65e24d6f2a6cf2ccba5cfb953bfde7ad1f2eab09f371cc32fed34.json is absent), Prestel et al. directly replicated the 39.5 cM D2S126-D2S125 autosomal dominant linkage model already represented by shipped row 1101 (Pankratz et al. 2003b, Ref 18, 10.1086/374383) and refer in the Discussion (line 233) to 'the original study by Pankratz et al' in the singular. corrected_value.title: Association of estrogen receptor gene polymorphisms with susceptibility to adolescent idiopathic scoliosis

decision.location: Background and Purpose, lines 4-6; see also Methods, Results, Conclusions and discussion, and References, lines 8-12
decision.quote:
It has been suggested that XbaI single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) (A/G rs934099) in estrogen receptor 1 (ESR1) may be associated with curve severity in Japanese AIS patients[ 1 ] and with both curve severity and predisposition for AIS in Chinese patients[ 2 ]. However, replication studies have not confirmed these findings[ 3 ]. The role of the XbaI ESR1 polymorphism rs9340799 in AIS has never been described in Caucasian AIS patients. 
 Purpose 
 A genetic association study was performed to investigate the association between XbaI SNP in ESR1 and the predisposition for, or progression of, AIS in Caucasian patients.
decision.reason: Janusz et al. (2013, 10.1186/1748-7161-8-s2-o2) explicitly re-test both previously reported ESR1 XbaI (rs9340799) associations in a Caucasian sample of 286 female AIS patients and 116 healthy female controls: (1) association with curve severity/progression/operation rate first reported in Japanese AIS patients by Inoue et al. (2002, 10.1097/00007632-200211010-00009, shipped row 2495, target_index 0), and (2) association with both predisposition (case-control susceptibility) for AIS and curve severity reported in Chinese AIS patients by Wu et al. (2006, Spine 31(10):1131-1136, 10.1097/01.brs.0000216603.91330.6f, candidate target_index 1). Janusz et al. empirically test case-control allele/genotype frequencies (predisposition/susceptibility: p=0.63 and p=0.35) as well as progression velocity, mean Cobb angle, and surgery rate, concluding that 'No association between ESR1 XbaI polymorphism and AIS was found in the Caucasian population. None of the previously reported associations with curve severity, progression or operation rate could be confirmed.' Wu et al. (2006) is an independent primary study by a distinct research group in a distinct cohort testing the susceptibility claim directly evaluated here, and it is absent from the shipped rows (which contain only Inoue et al. 2002, row 2495). Both listed prior adjudication/state files (b7f058b4...json and 5626af31...json) are absent.

decision.quote: In 2019, Schleu et al. showed that 400-m runners at major championships exhibited team effort gains-they ran faster in the relay than in the individual competition. However, due to low statistical power, it remains unclear whether these findings are replicable. In a replication and extension of this study, we wanted to find out whether its findings replicate in a sample of 1,718 observations from 1,270 U.S. college athletes and whether effort expenditure is driven by working in a team or the chance of valuable outcomes in the relay.
